notes.definition: Amino acids (Higher tier) are molecules with two different functional groups: an amine group (–NH₂) and a carboxylic acid group (–COOH). They react by condensation polymerisation to produce polypeptides, and different amino acids can be combined in the same chain to produce proteins.
explanation: An amino acid molecule contains two different functional groups. One end has an amine group, –NH₂, and the other end has a carboxylic acid group, –COOH. The simplest amino acid is glycine, H₂NCH₂COOH, in which the two groups are joined by a CH₂ group. Other amino acids have different groups in place of one of the hydrogen atoms on the central carbon, which gives each amino acid its own properties.

Because each amino acid has a reactive group at both ends, amino acids can join together by condensation polymerisation. The –COOH group of one amino acid reacts with the –NH₂ group of the next. The –OH from the acid group and an –H from the amine group are lost as a molecule of water, and a new link (–CO–NH–, called a peptide or amide link) forms between the two amino acids. This can happen again and again at both ends, building up a long chain called a polypeptide.

For glycine, the equation is: n H₂NCH₂COOH → –(HNCH₂CO)ₙ– + n H₂O. Each glycine unit forms one new link, so one water molecule is released for each repeating unit: n H₂O for n glycine molecules. Notice how this differs from a polyester made from a diol and a dicarboxylic acid: there, only one type of monomer is not enough, and 2n water molecules form per n repeating units. With amino acids, one type of monomer is enough because each molecule carries both kinds of functional group.

Different amino acids can be combined in the same chain. Proteins are polypeptides made from many amino acids joined in a particular order. There are about 20 different amino acids in living things, and the order in which they are joined decides the shape and job of the protein. Enzymes, haemoglobin, keratin in hair and the muscle protein in meat are all proteins made this way. When proteins are digested, the links are broken and the amino acids are released again.

When comparing with other polymers, remember: addition polymers come from monomers with a C=C double bond and give one product only. Condensation polymers come from monomers with two functional groups and also release water. Amino acids are special because each monomer has two different functional groups, so a single type of amino acid can form a polymer on its own.
keyFacts: Amino acids have two different functional groups: amine –NH₂ and carboxylic acid –COOH.
Glycine is the simplest amino acid: H₂NCH₂COOH.
Amino acids react by condensation polymerisation to form polypeptides.
–COOH of one amino acid reacts with –NH₂ of the next, losing H₂O.
One water molecule is released per link (n H₂O for n glycine).
Different amino acids can be combined in the same chain to produce proteins.
A single type of amino acid can polymerise because it has both functional groups.
The link formed is –CO–NH– (a peptide link).

keyTerms.definition: A molecule with an amine group (–NH₂) and a carboxylic acid group (–COOH).
A polymer made from amino acids joined by condensation polymerisation.
A naturally occurring polymer made from different amino acids joined in a particular order.
The –CO–NH– link formed when a –COOH group reacts with an –NH₂ group, releasing water.
Joining of monomers with two functional groups, with the loss of a small molecule such as water.

workedExamples.title: Mr of glycine and its repeating unit
workedExamples.question: Calculate the Mr of glycine, H₂NCH₂COOH, and of its repeating unit in the polypeptide. (Ar: H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16)
steps: Each glycine loses one H₂O (Mr 18) when it joins the chain.

workedExamples.title: Joining two amino acids
workedExamples.question: Show how two glycine molecules join and state what else forms.
steps: The –COOH of the first glycine reacts with the –NH₂ of the second.
OH from the acid and H from the amine are removed as H₂O.
A –CO–NH– link joins the molecules: H₂NCH₂CO–NHCH₂COOH.

workedExamples.title: Counting water molecules
workedExamples.question: A polypeptide is formed from 250 glycine molecules. Using the equation n H₂NCH₂COOH → –(HNCH₂CO)ₙ– + n H₂O, how many water molecules are released?

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think a polypeptide needs two different monomers, like a polyester.
misconceptions.right: In fact each amino acid has two different functional groups, so even one type of amino acid (such as glycine) can form a polymer.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think 2n water molecules form when n glycine molecules polymerise.
misconceptions.right: In fact each glycine forms one new link, so n H₂O are released (compare 2n H₂O for a diol and dicarboxylic acid polyester).

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think amino acids join by addition polymerisation.
misconceptions.right: In fact amino acids have no C=C bond; they join by condensation, releasing water.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think a protein is made of just one type of amino acid.
misconceptions.right: In fact proteins are made from many different amino acids combined in the same chain in a particular order.

realWorld: Your body joins about 20 different amino acids in specific orders to build proteins such as enzymes, antibodies and haemoglobin.
Digestion uses enzymes to break proteins in food back into amino acids, which are absorbed into the blood.
Silk and wool are natural protein fibres built from amino acids.
higherTier: All of this subtopic is Higher tier only (and separate Chemistry only): amino acids have two different functional groups, polymerise by condensation to form polypeptides, glycine equation, and proteins from different amino acids.
separateOnlyContent: Amino acids are only in separate Chemistry (8462), not Combined Science.
examTips: Name both functional groups in an amino acid: amine (–NH₂) and carboxylic acid (–COOH).
In the glycine equation, balance water as n H₂O, not 2n H₂O.
Check a repeating unit by atom counting: for glycine it is C₂H₃NO, which is glycine (C₂H₅NO₂) minus H₂O.
Use the term 'condensation polymerisation' and say water is lost when the –COOH and –NH₂ groups react.
summary: Amino acids have an amine group and a carboxylic acid group.
They polymerise by condensation, losing water.
Different amino acids combine to make proteins.

questions.question: Which two functional groups are found in every amino acid?
questions.explanation: Amino acids have an amine group and a carboxylic acid group. –OH and –COOH are in the diol and acid used for polyesters.

questions.question: What type of polymer is made when amino acids join together?
questions.explanation: Amino acids form polypeptides; proteins are polypeptides.

questions.question: Which small molecule is lost when two amino acids join?
questions.explanation: OH from the –COOH and H from the –NH₂ combine to form H₂O.

questions.question: What is the formula of glycine?
questions.explanation: Glycine has an –NH₂ group and a –COOH group joined by CH₂. CH₃COOH is ethanoic acid.

questions.question: What type of reaction joins amino acids together?
questions.explanation: A small molecule (water) is lost each time two amino acids join, so it is condensation.

questions.question: How are proteins different from a polypeptide made only from glycine?
options: Proteins are made from different amino acids combined in the same chain
Proteins are made by addition polymerisation
markScheme: 1 mark: different amino acids combined in the same chain
questions.explanation: Proteins are polypeptides made from many different amino acids in a particular order.

questions.question: When n glycine molecules polymerise, how many water molecules are formed?
questions.explanation: Each glycine forms one link with the next, releasing one water molecule: n H₂NCH₂COOH → –(HNCH₂CO)ₙ– + n H₂O.

questions.question: Which is the repeating unit of the polypeptide formed from glycine?
questions.explanation: One H is lost from –NH₂ and OH from –COOH, giving –HN–CH₂–CO– (C₂H₃NO).

questions.question: Why can glycine form a polymer on its own, while a polyester needs two different monomers?
options: Glycine has a C=C double bond
Glycine has two different functional groups that can react with each other
Glycine is a carboxylic acid only
Glycine is a larger molecule than a diol
markScheme: 1 mark: glycine has two different functional groups that react with each other
questions.explanation: The –NH₂ of one glycine reacts with the –COOH of another. A diol has only –OH groups, which cannot react with each other to form esters.

questions.question: Calculate the relative formula mass (Mr) of glycine, H₂NCH₂COOH. (Ar: H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16)
questions.explanation: 24 + 5 + 14 + 32 = 75. Count all five hydrogen atoms: two in NH₂, two in CH₂ and one in COOH.

questions.question: A polypeptide is made from 400 glycine molecules. Using the equation n H₂NCH₂COOH → –(HNCH₂CO)ₙ– + n H₂O, how many water molecules are released?
questions.explanation: The equation shows n water molecules for n glycine molecules.

questions.question: Calculate the Mr of the repeating unit –HNCH₂CO– in the polypeptide made from glycine (Mr of glycine = 75, Mr of water = 18).
questions.explanation: Each glycine loses one water molecule when it joins the chain, so the unit has Mr 57 (C₂H₃NO: 24 + 3 + 14 + 16 = 57).

questions.question: Two glycine molecules (Mr = 75) join to form a dipeptide and water. Calculate the Mr of the dipeptide. (Mr of H₂O = 18)
questions.explanation: Two molecules form one link, so only one water molecule is lost: H₂NCH₂CONHCH₂COOH, Mr 132.

questions.question: A polypeptide chain contains 300 repeating units of –HNCH₂CO– (Mr of each unit = 57). Calculate the total Mr of the repeating units.
questions.explanation: Multiply the number of units by the Mr of one unit: 300 × 57 = 17 100.

questions.question: Name the simplest amino acid.
questions.explanation: Glycine, H₂NCH₂COOH, has just a CH₂ group between the amine and acid groups.

questions.question: Name the two functional groups in an amino acid.
questions.explanation: The name 'amino acid' comes from these two groups.

questions.question: State what type of natural polymer is made when many different amino acids join together.
questions.explanation: Different amino acids combined in the same chain make proteins.

questions.question: Describe what happens to the functional groups when two amino acid molecules join.
acceptedAnswers: OH from acid, H from amine
markScheme: 1 mark: the –COOH group of one amino acid reacts with the –NH₂ group of the other
1 mark: OH and H are removed as water, forming a –CO–NH– link
questions.explanation: This is a condensation reaction: two molecules join and water is released.

questions.question: Write the equation for the polymerisation of glycine, using n.
questions.explanation: n monomers form n repeating units and n water molecules.

questions.question: Explain why the polymerisation of amino acids is described as condensation polymerisation.
markScheme: 1 mark: monomers have two functional groups and join to form a polymer
1 mark: a small molecule (water) is lost each time a link forms
questions.explanation: Condensation reactions release a small molecule as two molecules join.

questions.question: Alanine is an amino acid with the formula H₂NCH(CH₃)COOH. Write the formula of the dipeptide formed when one glycine molecule (H₂NCH₂COOH) reacts with one alanine molecule through the –COOH group of glycine.
markScheme: 1 mark: –CO–NH– link between the glycine carbonyl and alanine nitrogen
questions.explanation: Glycine's –COOH loses OH and alanine's –NH₂ loses H, giving water and the dipeptide.

questions.question: Compare the number of water molecules produced when (a) n glycine molecules polymerise and (b) n diol molecules react with n dicarboxylic acid molecules. Explain the difference.
markScheme: 1 mark: each glycine repeating unit contains one link, whereas each polyester repeating unit contains two links (one diol and one acid)
questions.explanation: Count the links per repeating unit: one for glycine, two for the polyester.

questions.question: Describe how amino acids form polypeptides and proteins. Use glycine as an example.
markScheme: Indicative content: amino acids have amine (–NH₂) and carboxylic acid (–COOH) groups; glycine is H₂NCH₂COOH; –COOH of one reacts with –NH₂ of the next; water is lost; condensation polymerisation; long chain called a polypeptide; n H₂NCH₂COOH → –(HNCH₂CO)ₙ– + n H₂O; different amino acids combined in the same chain form proteins.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): functional groups named, the reaction described with water lost, and proteins linked to different amino acids.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements, e.g. amino acids join to make proteins.
questions.explanation: Include both functional groups, the condensation reaction and the link to proteins.

questions.question: Compare the formation of poly(ethene), a polyester and a polypeptide. Refer to the monomers, functional groups, type of polymerisation, other products and how many types of monomer are needed.
markScheme: Indicative content: poly(ethene): monomer ethene with C=C; addition polymerisation; one type of monomer; no other product; repeating unit same atoms as monomer. Polyester: diol (two –OH) and dicarboxylic acid (two –COOH); two different monomers each with two of the same group; condensation; ester links; 2n H₂O. Polypeptide: amino acids with two different functional groups (–NH₂ and –COOH); one type (e.g. glycine) can polymerise alone, or different amino acids give proteins; condensation; n H₂O for n glycine; –CO–NH– links.
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): accurate comparison of all three polymers covering monomers, functional groups, polymerisation type and products, with correct water ratios.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): compares at least two polymers in detail, or all three with some errors.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements about one or two polymers.
questions.explanation: Organise the answer feature by feature so each comparison is clear.

questions.question: Which element is found in amino acids but not in carboxylic acids or alcohols?
questions.explanation: The amine group, –NH₂, contains nitrogen.

questions.question: State the general type of molecule that proteins are made from.
questions.explanation: Proteins are polymers of amino acids.
